title: Reject readings too large for one producer deadline at reading time
summary: Root cause: reading validation (build_reading in athena-core/src/reading.rs) never compares a reading's scope with the producer and verifier deadlines in athena.toml, so multi-item sources yield readings no single run can finish. Add a deterministic size gate there that rejects a reading whose own forecast wall time p50 exceeds the configured producer or verifier timeout. The rejection tells the reader to pick one deliverable and name the rest as follow-up requests. Audience: Athena maintainers and the reader loop, which gets a clear retry message.

defaults_applied.how: The size rule is enforced by code in build_reading, not by prose alone.
Unit tests added; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Fix at reading validation, which every job passes through, not at one job.
Tests feed oversized and fitting readings through build_reading and check the outcome.
One gate in one module plus tests and a changelog line.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The gate uses existing config (limits.producer_timeout_s, verifier_timeout_s) so no athena.toml change is needed.
The reader's own forecast wall_time_s.p50 is the available size signal; a p50 above the deadline means the reader itself expects to overrun.
A rejected reading goes through the existing 'reader's output was invalid' retry path, bounded by max_readings.
Reader prompt text is a secondary hint only; the mechanism is the code check.

acceptance_criteria.text: The change description names the root cause: reading validation never compares reading scope with the producer/verifier deadline, and the fix sits in build_reading in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs.

A new unit test in athena-core builds a reading whose forecast wall_time_s.p50 exceeds limits.producer_timeout_s and asserts build_reading returns an error whose message tells the reader to pick one deliverable and name the rest as follow-up requests. Run cargo test -p athena-core.

A companion test shows a reading with p50 within the deadlines is still accepted, and the oversize test fails if the gate is removed. The tests use a generic oversize forecast, not one job's data. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo test --workspace all pass.
CHANGELOG.md records the new reading size gate.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml limits or adding new config keys
Retry-scope tracking across jobs or re-ask handling
urgent_reason: Cuts repeated producer and verifier deadline timeouts and rejected or retried attempts caused by oversized readings.
hard_reason: Changes the reading gate that decides which readings Athena accepts for all jobs.
